chunk_map.heading: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps
Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 line 7: 'Before this module edits files or cuts rules, decide whether it is done enough, should be stopped, or counts as the partial artefact.' -- 'the partial artefact' and 'M5's session' read as never-named on a cold read of this file alone, BUT the enclosing module file (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md line 24, '## Start here', which renders BEFORE this exercise in both deck and long-read) already states: 'before it writes, decide whether to wait, stop M5, or accept the partial session as the artefact.' Per rule 1's module-include-order carve-out ('vocabulary the enclosing module file's signposting introduced counts as prior context for the exercises it includes'), this resolves -- prior context, not a dangling referent. Second judgment call: chunk 2 line 29 'the quote rule re-asserted' -- not verbatim-named anywhere, but chunk 1's prompt (line 24 expansion) states 'For every claim, quote a specific moment from the artefacts. Don't generalise,' one slide back and the only candidate a deck reader would map it to -- passes as a natural shorthand for content just read, not a second/ambiguous candidate. Remaining referents (task.md, plan.md, Run coordinates, the packaging, the verifier, ./CLAUDE.local.md, the diff in chunk 4) each resolve to either the immediately preceding chunk or to vocabulary the M4/M5 module files establish before this exercise (verified via grep of curriculum/exercises/fork-the-worktree.md:39 for 'Run coordinates').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -noE 'the [a-zA-Z-]+ you (did|saw|caught|found|wrote|built|made|just [a-z]+)' on the body: no output. The only backward-pointing beats named are M4 and M5 (chunks 0-1: 'the un-packaged Module 4 send-off', 'M5's session', 'the m4/<slug> branch', 'the m5/<slug> branch') -- both confirmed present in the training's current module set via site/layouts/curriculum.js TRAININGS['agentic-engineering-101'].modules (run-the-first-experiment = M4, learn-from-the-test = M5, both listed immediately before this file's own module spot-gaps-build-the-loop = M6). No dead-beat shape found.

Chunks 1-4 each carry a self-contained instruction plus either a prompt card or an explicit decision rule (chunk 4: 'Push back if the diff touches more than the one rule you flagged... One rule cut, no more.'). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Each header matches its chunk's content under sequential read: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (chunk 1) both diffs and asks to rank via the prompt's closing line 'which gap matters most? Rank by damage-to-a-future-session'; 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' (chunk 2) matches its three push-back bullets; 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (chunk 3) matches the cut-prompt; 'Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (chunk 4) matches the approve/push-back bullets. No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all five sub-items against every chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (closest is chunk 0 line 13 'two sessions are enough to place every lesson', a substantive teaching claim about the method, not a claim the exercise is valuable/impressive); no number-with-retraction pattern (no numbers appear in body prose outside the Time: label); no abstraction-noun stack (vocabulary throughout is concrete: branch, worktree, transcript, rules file); no empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|Connections)\b' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--spot-gaps-build-the-loop.body.txt (the numbered body projection, maintainer/backing tail excluded by construction) -> no matches. Vocabulary throughout (branch, worktree, transcript, diff, rules file, verifier, plan) is ordinary engineer register.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest-to-violating case: chunk 0 (title slide, lines 3-13) carries five separate bolded labels -- **Time:**, **Session**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:** -- naively over a naive '<=1 bolded element per slide' count. Each is a <=2-word label/chrome bullet, not a bolded lead sentence, and this exact five-label shape ('**Time:**' as the opening bold) appears in 40 of the corpus's exercise files (grep -l '^\*\*Time:\*\*' curriculum/exercises/*.md), so the count is the exercise-file template's doing, structurally identical to the WYL-bullets and task-sizing exceptions this rule already names ('check whether another rule or the module template requires the bold you are about to charge for'). Maintainer accept-note at L56 (Emphasis pass, 2026-07-09) independently confirms the intent for this file: 'bullet leads plain; bold only on widget / label chrome.' Chunks 1-4 carry zero bold markup (grep confirms no '**' outside chunk 0 and the maintainer tail).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: signals.slide_count: 4 matches a manual count of '##' headings in the raw body (4), confirming nothing silently dropped from the composed deck. The whole body sits inside the standard exercise structure (no top-level prose outside a '##' chunk or the pre-first-heading title slide), and this file renders under the module's own '.phase--exercise' wrapper by the same mechanism every AE101 exercise uses -- not something this file's own content could opt out of. The diff since the pin (4589f1d5) touched only bullet/maintainer prose (git diff 4589f1d5..HEAD), no tier marker, phase marker, or heading, so deck presence is unaffected by this revision.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size -- 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md -> 'files: 1  slides: 4  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets  oversized: 0' / '✓ every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four body headings are imperative exercise-shape constructions, none declarative: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (line 17), 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' (line 26), 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (line 32), 'Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (line 41). This exercise is diagnostic/procedural throughout and never reaches a stated law that would call for a declarative heading, so the claim-heading requirement for law/consolidation slides does not apply here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest-to-violating case: chunk 3 line 35 'Rules-files have a half-life. Adding rules is only half of it; subtracting the dead ones is the other half.' -- reads as a general-sounding claim but it is the FIRST and only statement of this framing anywhere in the file (not a doctrine re-announcement, class (a)), it is not self-referential design commentary (class (b): it is about rules-files, not about the training's own pedagogy), and it does not close the chunk (the prompt card follows it) so it is not an aphorism kicker (class (c)). It earns its slot by supplying the rationale ('a priority') for the cut the next line asks for. No instance of any of the three named classes found elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: git diff 4e0370bc..HEAD on this file changes only bullet/prose text, no '##' heading line; maintainer block carries no provenance note of the '(from <old-file>, header ...)' shape. Neither trigger condition for this rule is present.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -noE '\[.*\]\(' on the body: no output (matches signals.has_urls: false). Body carries zero markdown links, so the cross-file-callback-by-position shape this rule targets does not occur. The M4/M5 references (chunk 0-1) name the source directly ('M5 worktree', 'm4/<slug> branch', 'task.md', 'plan.md') rather than locating it by position ('the previous module said'), so even read generously they don't trip this rule; that resolution sits under §1's carve-outs, not §2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body -- this is a diagnose-and-diff exercise (compare two sessions, cut one rule), not a live-demo beat that narrates an outcome and then asks the student to guess it.
